authority: CEO Round 156: 'The next iteration should force every promising candidate to answer four hostile questions: Does it work? Was it already obvious? Does it beat the best alternative? Can the buyer reproduce it without us? Only when the answer to all four is favorable should the machine even consider WORLD_CLASS_INVENTION.'
constitutional_basis: Article I — evidence precedes assertion (each question requires evidence)
Article VII — never weaken the verifier to rescue a claim (cannot weaken the questions)
Article XVII — every control must have an attempted bypass (the questions ARE the bypass attempt)
Article XIX — never optimize for the gate (the questions must be answered favorably in reality, not in presentation)
Article XXVIII — no silent semantic promotion (answering 'works in simulation' is not 'works')
Article XXXII — state strongest alternative (Q3 requires this)
the_four_hostile_questions: Q3: Does it beat the best alternative?
Q4: Can the buyer reproduce it without us?
evaluation_rule: WORLD_CLASS_INVENTION only when the answer to ALL FOUR questions is FAVORABLE. A weak answer on any one question blocks promotion. The questions are hostile — they are designed to find reasons the candidate should NOT be promoted.

C2_Y_HOSTILE_QUESTIONS.candidate: C2-Y: Longitudinal Shunt Response-Manifold Failure Prediction

Q1_DOES_IT_WORK.question: Does C2-Y actually provide clinically meaningful lead time for shunt failure prediction, at acceptable false-alarm rate, across all major failure modes?
evidence_required: C2-Y-R1 experiment results showing lead time >= 24h at FPR = 1 FA/patient-month on EACH of 5 failure modes
Calibration error within acceptable bounds (Brier score < 0.15)
Robustness index showing lead-time degradation < 30% under sensor drift / model mismatch / patient transfer
Q1_DOES_IT_WORK.current_answer: UNKNOWN — experiment has not yet been run
Q1_DOES_IT_WORK.if_experiment_succeeds: Answer becomes FAVORABLE (with explicit provenance to C2-Y-R1 results)
Q1_DOES_IT_WORK.if_experiment_fails: Answer becomes UNFAVORABLE → C2-Y cannot be promoted
Q1_DOES_IT_WORK.if_experiment_is_inconclusive: Answer remains UNKNOWN → C2-Y remains in INVESTIGATION (Article XXXIII — no irreversible action on unresolved evidence)

Q2_WAS_IT_ALREADY_OBVIOUS.question: Was C2-Y's response-manifold deviation method already obvious from published prior art?
evidence_required: Claim-level §102/§103 patent novelty analysis
Search for prior art on response-manifold deviation in shunt/physiological monitoring context
Search for prior art on latent degradation prediction in medical devices generally
Search for academic publications proposing similar methods
Q2_WAS_IT_ALREADY_OBVIOUS.current_answer: UNKNOWN — full patent novelty analysis has not yet been done
Q2_WAS_IT_ALREADY_OBVIOUS.what_we_know: Perturbation testing is PRIOR_ART_KNOWN (VIEshunt, PMID 26208258, 27203135). The specific concept of LONGITUDINAL LATENT-DEGRADATION PREDICTION FROM RESPONSE-MANIFOLD DEVIATION has not been found in our prior art search, but the search has not been exhaustive.
Q2_WAS_IT_ALREADY_OBVIOUS.if_novel: Answer becomes FAVORABLE (with explicit patent novelty analysis)
Q2_WAS_IT_ALREADY_OBVIOUS.if_obvious: Answer becomes UNFAVORABLE → C2-Y cannot be promoted (Article VII — cannot weaken patent analysis to rescue claim)

Q3_DOES_IT_BEAT_THE_BEST_ALTERNATIVE.question: Does C2-Y beat the strongest publicly plausible alternative (UISB = VIEshunt + Nature ICP + Codman threshold)?
evidence_required: C2-Y-R1 experiment results showing C2-Y beats UISB on primary endpoint (lead time at fixed FPR)
C2-Y-R2 independent reproduction showing the result is not over-fit to our internal simulator (Article XXVIII)
C2-Y-R3 design-around attack showing simple alternative (threshold on response deviation) does NOT achieve similar performance — i.e., C2-Y's specific method has moat
Q3_DOES_IT_BEAT_THE_BEST_ALTERNATIVE.current_answer: UNKNOWN — experiments have not yet been run
Q3_DOES_IT_BEAT_THE_BEST_ALTERNATIVE.strongest_alternative_explanation_to_sta: Per Article XXXII: VIEshunt's commercializer or Medtronic may have undisclosed chronic + prediction R&D. C2-Y beating the UISB (publicly plausible baseline) is NOT the same as beating the true incumbent.
Q3_DOES_IT_BEAT_THE_BEST_ALTERNATIVE.if_beats_UISB: Answer becomes FAVORABLE for publicly plausible baseline. Does NOT prove beating undisclosed incumbent R&D.
Q3_DOES_IT_BEAT_THE_BEST_ALTERNATIVE.if_does_not_beat_UISB: Answer becomes UNFAVORABLE → C2-Y cannot be promoted

Q4_CAN_THE_BUYER_REPRODUCE_IT_WITHOUT_US.question: Can the buyer (CereVasc, Medtronic, Integra, Sophysa, VIEshunt commercializer) reproduce C2-Y's capability without acquiring us?
evidence_required: Patent protection analysis (do we have patents that block reproduction?)
Trade secret analysis (is there know-how that is not publicly disclosed?)
Validation data analysis (do we have proprietary clinical data that competitors cannot easily generate?)
Workflow integration analysis (is C2-Y integrated with specific hardware/workflow that creates switching cost?)
Q4_CAN_THE_BUYER_REPRODUCE_IT_WITHOUT_US.current_answer: UNKNOWN — patent, trade secret, validation data, and workflow integration have not been analyzed
what_would_make_buyer_unable_to_reproduc: Strong patent on specific response-manifold method
Workflow integration with specific hardware (eShunt, Codman valve, etc.) creating switching cost
Regulatory clearance creating moat (FDA SaMD pathway)
what_would_make_buyer_able_to_reproduce: No patent or weak patent (response-manifold is a generic concept)
Q4_CAN_THE_BUYER_REPRODUCE_IT_WITHOUT_US.if_buyer_cannot_reproduce: Answer becomes FAVORABLE (with explicit moat analysis)
Q4_CAN_THE_BUYER_REPRODUCE_IT_WITHOUT_US.if_buyer_can_reproduce: Answer becomes UNFAVORABLE → C2-Y's moat is weak → re-evaluate acquisition thesis

the_strongest_moat_definition.quote: The strongest version is: a technical capability that an incumbent can buy but cannot cheaply reproduce. That is exactly what you should aim for if the eventual goal is acquisition/licensing.
the_strongest_moat_definition.operationalization: For each candidate, the answer to Q4 ('Can the buyer reproduce it without us?') must be UNFAVORABLE TO THE BUYER (i.e., the buyer CANNOT easily reproduce). If the buyer can easily reproduce, the candidate is not acquirable.
tests_for_irreproducibility: Independent reproduction moat (Article XXVIII — most competitors use single solver; if we have multi-world, that is a moat)

summary.current_state: ALL four hostile questions for ALL three candidates (C2-Y, C3-X, C5-X) are UNKNOWN. No candidate can be promoted to World-Class.
summary.what_is_needed_for_promotion: Each candidate must achieve FAVORABLE on all four hostile questions. This requires running the experiments (C2-Y-R1, C3-X-R1, C5-X-R1), the patent novelty analysis, the design-around attacks, and the moat analysis.
summary.honest_acknowledgment: The four hostile questions framework is the right framework, but answering all four favorably is a high bar. None of the three candidates is close to answering all four. World-Class = 0/5 remains the correct state.
